rulings.Case Title: GUARDIANSHIP OF KEVIN HU
rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION FOR TERMINATION OF GUARDIANSHIP of Person
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 9/15/26 to address the following issues: 1. The petition is not verified by the guardian. An unverified pleading may be proved by filing a supplemental declaration that identifies the pleading by caption and its filing date [Local Rule 14.15C]. 2. The waiver of account indicates that it is regarding a decedent's estate. A new waiver of account must be filed properly identifying it as regarding the former minor's guardianship estate. 3. The petition does not state what is in the account and what is to be distributed to the former minor. An amendment to the petition must be filed (verified by the petitioner) specifying the amount in the bank account, as of a date certain, that will be distributed to the former minor. The bank statement that verifies the amount should also be filed. Notice of Hearing on filing of the amendment must be provided on the former minor. 4. Proposed order has not been filed. All documents to be filed by 8/31/26.

rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF PRIMROSE AGNES CHAO
rulings.Calendar Matter: ACCOUNTING PETITION RE: Fees, Final Distribution
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 9/2/2026. The Court will not order compensation to be paid from the personal representative's own funds, regardless of the stipulation. If the beneficiary wishes to distribute property without selling it, and insufficient liquid assets remain to pay compensation, that beneficiary may advance funds to the estate. This allows the Court to order fees to be paid from estate funds. The advancement can be reported as a miscellaneous acquisition of property and must not be added to the fee base. The petition needs to be amended accordingly. Otherwise, need for authority under which the Court can order the personal funds to pay the fees.

rulings.Case Title: IN THE MATTER OF THE PARSONS TRUST DATED JULY 23, 2002, AS AMENDED AND RESTATED ON OCTOBER 7, 2019 AND AMENDED ON AUG
rulings.Calendar Matter: ADDED TO CALENDAR FOR Petition For Appointment Of Successor Trustee Due To Vacancy In The Office Of Trustee And To Set Trust Bond
rulings.Rulings: Hearing. Appearance required. The judicial officer is to review and determine, and counsel and parties may be asked to address: 1) Does Neyola Parsons have sufficient capacity to express her preference as to who should manage her trust as successor trustee? Neyola personally signed and verified this petition as the sole petitioner requesting appointment of her nephew Joseph Belarde (and not her niece/objector Denise Parsons). The only person named as successor trustee in the second amendment as the operative trust is the settlor's caregiver Anna Alvarado. The first amendment that named the objector Denise Parsons as successor trustee remains superseded by the second amendment, unless and until the second amendment challenged by Denise as the product of undue influence by the caregiver Anna is judicially declared invalid. In light of the caregiver Anna's declination to serve as trustee on file, the office of trustee is vacant within the meaning of Article 3.03(d) of the trust which allows Neyola as "the surviving Settlor" or "the trust's Primary Beneficiary" (defined in Article 17.08(h) & (o)) to nominate a trustee of her choice. More importantly, Article 8.01 of the trust allows Neyola as the surviving Settlor to remove and replace the trustee at any time, with or without cause. 2) If Neyola lacks sufficient capacity to express her preference, does Neyola's conservator Melissa Chung consent to Joseph Belarde serving as general successor trustee as proposed by this petition? The conservatee Neyola's rights as the surviving settlor to remove, replace, and appoint trustees should be exercisable by Melissa Chung as Neyola's conservator. While Article 8.02 of the trust evidences an intent under Probate Code section 2580(b)(11) to prohibit the conservator from petitioning for substituted judgment to exercise Neyola's right to amend her trust, Article 8.01 does not prohibit the conservator from exercising Neyola's right to choose a trustee. 3) Immediate steps must be taken by the objector Denise to remove Neyola's unredacted social security number and date of birth from her objection on file (Exhibit J, pages 70 & 72), as the protected information remains viewable online by the general public. PARTIES APPEARING SHOULD CHECK IN FOR THE HEARING WITH THEIR FULL NAME. Counsel and parties may appear personally or remotely through Zoom or CourtCall. For a video appearance, go to zoom.us, click "join a meeting" and input meeting ID 160 225 4765 and password 514879. For an audio-only appearance through Zoom, call 1-669-254-5252 and key in meeting ID "160 225 4765#", then participant ID "0#", then password "514879#". (Toll rates may apply).) The Court prefers that counsel and parties appearing by video input their first and last name into the "Your Name" dialogue box. Counsel and parties may appear by audio-only telephone through CourtCall by calling 1-888-882-6878. Please review LRSF 14.1(C) for more information.
